verdict.rationale: Community hands-on evidence says AutoGen runs agent-generated code in a fresh Docker container by default, which is the product's own sandboxed-execution capability, and AutoGen Studio documents running teams in a Docker container. Nothing in the pack shows fine-grained tool permissions such as allowlists, per-tool scopes or approval policies. missing for 10: fine-grained tool permission controls, first-party documentation of the sandboxed code-execution configuration and its isolation guarantees.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can restrict what an agent may do with fine-grained tool permissions and sandboxed execution

citations.quote: autogen creates a new docker container each time code is executed by agents (default behaviour, can be turned off)
